claim: Screens become the preferred visual-art medium
originalWording: Screens become the preferred visual-art medium

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Computer screens become the prevailing medium for visual-art creation/presentation, with intelligent software collaboration.
strict.rationale: Digital art tools were established, but the broad claim of preference across visual art was stronger than the evidence of availability. AI art receives serious recognition, yet painting, sculpture, print and physical display remain important; there is no defensible universal medium-of-choice ranking here.

evidence.title: Christie’s: Human-machine art collaboration at auction
evidence.note: Obvious/GAN portrait sold October 2018 for $432,500. Supports serious institutional attention, not majority adoption by artists.

broader.criterion: Digital screens and intelligent tools become the prevailing high-volume medium for visual art creation and viewing, while physical art remains valued.
broader.rationale: Digital art software existed in 2009, but screen-based visual creation, distribution, and AI-assisted art only became the dominant everyday visual medium during the 2010s–2020s (marked institutionally by Christie's 2018 sale and subsequent digital/AI art ubiquity).
changedConditions: Relaxes exclusive preference across traditional fine art to dominant volume medium in the 2010s–2020s
